scenarios.title: SCN-0c setup (not a scenario): the three judges prove their mailbox through the real sign-in link; the owner does too (reading no-shows needs it)
SCN-12.1 ordinal competition: scoring set up and published, four entries paid, running order published, panel ready, heat on the floor
SCN-10.1 no-show: the official marks the last entry as no-show in the active heat
SCN-10.5 judge sheet: the no-show entry is gone from the ranking form, with a note
SCN-12.2 ordinal ballots: three judges rank the three entries who danced from their own accounts
SCN-12.3 lock: the manager locks the ordinal ballots (or the desk states exactly why it cannot)
SCN-10.4 after the ballots lock, marking a no-show is refused and the controls are gone
SCN-6.3 official scratch in a locked heat: with HL1 a heat locks only after it is danced, so the scratch page refuses it as danced (the official locked-heat path is not reachable)
scenarios.note: The official scratch in a locked, not-yet-danced heat (SC1 path official_locked) is unreachable: HL1 offers Lock heat only for a danced heat, and a danced and locked heat is classed as danced, which the scratch page refuses. The refusal ('This entry has already danced. Changes go through the results correction workflow.') is asserted and no scratch is written.

scenarios.title: SCN-14.1 calculate: the result ranks the entries who danced, excludes the no-show, and a calculator-only approval is refused
SCN-14.2 correction: the manager opens a correction; the judge sheet shows the correction banner and takes a corrected ballot with a reason (CX1)
SCN-14.2b a corrected ballot makes the result stale: it cannot be approved until it is recalculated
SCN-14.3 recalculate and approve: a second manager approves, the heat is certified, and a certified heat refuses a scratch
SCN-14.4 who can see results: judges, the other studio, the instructor, and anonymous visitors cannot open them; the public event page shows none
SCN-13.1 publication: the dancer sees only their own entries and the published placements; a correction republishes as v2
